description: A chief legal officer must approve the company's response to an FDA warning letter about online product claims, including the response path, claim withdrawals, corrective-action verification, product-distribution treatment, and recall position, with input from regulatory counsel and the quality liaison.

shared_context.S1: The FDA issued a warning letter concerning three efficacy claims on the company's consumer product website.
shared_context.S2: The company has received no reports of patient injury associated with the product.
shared_context.S3: Mara Chen has final authority to approve the written response and its operational commitments.
shared_context.S4: At the firm's weekly regulatory-response huddle, Mara reviews the proposed package after regulatory counsel and quality representatives report any relevant developments.

PF1.text: Elias received an FDA email after the last response-team review offering informal resolution if the company withdraws exactly the three claims identified in the warning letter and verifies corrective-action completion within exactly 90 days; he has not entered the email in the response tracker yet.

PF2.text: Nina confirmed with quality operations yesterday that the FDA has not requested a product recall and that the company's approved risk plan permits continued distribution to pediatric clinics while the three claims are removed from labeling and web materials; she has not added that confirmation to the response tracker.

acceptance_conditions: The response must use the FDA's informal-resolution path.
The response must withdraw exactly the three claims identified in the warning letter.
Corrective-action completion must be verified within exactly 90 days.
Distribution must continue to pediatric clinics during the corrective-action period.
No product recall may be initiated.
The informal-resolution offer must be cited as justification for the response path and exact corrective-action terms.

decisive_facts.why: Without the FDA's informal-resolution offer, the response would not require the exact informal path, withdrawal of claims 1 through 3, or exactly 90-day corrective-action verification.
Without the quality confirmation, the response would not establish the specific pediatric-clinic distribution continuation or the decision not to initiate a recall.
